atoms.text: This guide configures a bucket to receive network flow logs from the FlowTrace service for account 111122223333. Create a bucket named example-flow-logs in the same Region as the monitored virtual networks, and leave Block Public Access enabled. Attach a bucket policy with a statement whose Sid is FlowTraceDeliveryWrite and whose Effect is Allow. Set the Principal to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/FlowTraceDeliveryRole, which your team created and which writes the flow records. Set Action to s3:PutObject and Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-flow-logs/flowtrace/AWSLogs/111122223333/*. Add a Condition using StringEquals on s3:x-amz-acl with the value bucket-owner-full-control, so that the bucket owner retains control of each delivered object. A second statement allows the same role to call s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket, which is used to verify the destination before the first delivery. After saving the policy, enable flow logging on a virtual network and confirm that compressed log files appear under the prefix within about ten minutes.

This guide configures a bucket to receive network flow logs from the FlowTrace service for account 111122223333. Create a bucket named example-flow-logs in the same Region as the monitored virtual networks, and leave Block Public Access enabled. Attach a bucket policy with a statement whose Sid is FlowTraceDeliveryWrite and whose Effect is Allow. Set the Principal to the service principal flowtrace.amazonaws.com, which is the identity FlowTrace uses when it writes the flow records. Set Action to s3:PutObject and Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-flow-logs/flowtrace/AWSLogs/111122223333/*. Add Conditions using StringEquals on s3:x-amz-acl with the value bucket-owner-full-control and on aws:SourceAccount with the value 111122223333, so that only deliveries from your account are accepted and the bucket owner retains control of each object. A second statement allows the same service principal to call s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket, which is used to verify the destination before the first delivery. After saving the policy, enable flow logging on a virtual network and confirm that compressed log files appear under the prefix within about ten minutes.

This procedure prepares a bucket to hold API audit trail files produced by the AuditLedger service. Create a bucket named example-audit-trail and enable versioning so that overwritten or deleted log files remain recoverable. Add a bucket policy statement with the Sid AuditLedgerAclCheck that allows s3:GetBucketAcl on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-trail. The Principal for this statement is the IAM user arn:aws:iam::444455556666:user/auditledger-writer, a dedicated identity whose credentials are held by the trail configuration. Add a second statement with the Sid AuditLedgerWrite that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-trail/ledger/AWSLogs/444455556666/* for the same IAM user. Require the condition StringEquals on s3:x-amz-acl set to bucket-owner-full-control in the write statement. Create the trail and select example-audit-trail as the destination, with ledger as the prefix. Verify delivery by listing the prefix after the first event batch, which normally arrives within fifteen minutes.

This procedure prepares a bucket to hold API audit trail files produced by the AuditLedger service. Create a bucket named example-audit-trail and enable versioning so that overwritten or deleted log files remain recoverable. Add a bucket policy statement with the Sid AuditLedgerAclCheck that allows s3:GetBucketAcl on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-trail. The Principal for this statement is the service principal auditledger.amazonaws.com, with an aws:SourceArn condition matching the trail ARN arn:aws:auditledger:us-east-1:444455556666:trail/main. Add a second statement with the Sid AuditLedgerWrite that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-trail/ledger/AWSLogs/444455556666/* for the same service principal. Require the condition StringEquals on s3:x-amz-acl set to bucket-owner-full-control in the write statement, together with the same source ARN condition. Create the trail and select example-audit-trail as the destination, with ledger as the prefix. Verify delivery by listing the prefix after the first event batch, which normally arrives within fifteen minutes.

This section describes how to store access logs from an EdgeBalancer load balancer in a bucket. The bucket, example-lb-access-logs, must reside in the same Region as the load balancer. Add a bucket policy statement with the Sid LoadBalancerLogWrite and Effect Allow. Set the Principal to arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/EdgeBalancerLogRole, a role in the account that owns the load balancer. Set Action to s3:PutObject and Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-lb-access-logs/edge/AWSLogs/777788889999/*. Do not grant s3:GetObject or s3:DeleteObject in this statement, since the delivery path only writes. In the load balancer attributes, turn on access logging and enter the bucket name and the prefix edge. The load balancer writes a test file on activation, and a failure to write returns a permissions error that you can resolve by checking the Resource ARN.

This section describes how to store access logs from an EdgeBalancer load balancer in a bucket. The bucket, example-lb-access-logs, must reside in the same Region as the load balancer. Add a bucket policy statement with the Sid LoadBalancerLogWrite and Effect Allow. Set the Principal to the service principal logdelivery.edgebalancer.amazonaws.com, and add an aws:SourceAccount condition with the value 777788889999. Set Action to s3:PutObject and Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-lb-access-logs/edge/AWSLogs/777788889999/*. Do not grant s3:GetObject or s3:DeleteObject in this statement, since the delivery path only writes. In the load balancer attributes, turn on access logging and enter the bucket name and the prefix edge. The load balancer writes a test file on activation, and a failure to write returns a permissions error that you can resolve by checking the Resource ARN.

These steps allow CDN request logs from the EdgeCache distribution to be written to a bucket. Create the bucket example-cdn-logs and set its object ownership to bucket owner enforced, which disables ACLs. Edit the bucket policy and add a statement with the Sid CdnStandardLogs and Effect Allow. Use the Principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/EdgeCacheLogWriter, a role in the distribution's account. Allow the action s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-cdn-logs/cache-logs/*. Restrict the statement with an IpAddress condition limited to the egress range 203.0.113.0/24 used by your log pipeline. In the distribution settings, enable standard logging, select the bucket, and set the prefix to cache-logs/. Each log file is gzip-compressed and named with the distribution ID and a timestamp. Allow up to an hour before the first file appears, as records are batched before they are written.

These steps allow CDN request logs from the EdgeCache distribution to be written to a bucket. Create the bucket example-cdn-logs and set its object ownership to bucket owner enforced, which disables ACLs. Edit the bucket policy and add a statement with the Sid CdnStandardLogs and Effect Allow. Use the service principal delivery.edgecache.amazonaws.com, which is the identity that delivers logs for distributions. Allow the action s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-cdn-logs/cache-logs/*. Restrict the statement with an ArnLike condition on aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:edgecache::123456789012:distribution/*, so only your distributions can write. In the distribution settings, enable standard logging, select the bucket, and set the prefix to cache-logs/. Each log file is gzip-compressed and named with the distribution ID and a timestamp. Allow up to an hour before the first file appears, as records are batched before they are written.

This guide covers delivery of DNS query logs from ResolverLog to a bucket for later analysis. Create a bucket named example-dns-query-logs and apply a lifecycle rule that expires objects after 90 days. Add a policy statement with the Sid ResolverLogDelivery that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-dns-query-logs/resolver/*. Set the Principal to the AWS account 210987654321, which owns the resolver and performs the delivery from within that account. Add s3:GetBucketLocation as an additional action on the bucket ARN so the delivery job can confirm the Region. Add a StringEquals condition on s3:x-amz-acl with bucket-owner-full-control. Create a query logging configuration in ResolverLog, associate it with the target virtual network, and specify the bucket ARN with the resolver prefix. Query records are written as newline-delimited JSON files, and you can validate delivery by opening the newest object.

Set the Principal to the service principal resolverlog.amazonaws.com, with an aws:SourceAccount condition set to 210987654321 to confine delivery to your resolver. Add s3:GetBucketLocation as an additional action on the bucket ARN so the delivery job can confirm the Region. Add a StringEquals condition on s3:x-amz-acl with bucket-owner-full-control. Create a query logging configuration in ResolverLog, associate it with the target virtual network, and specify the bucket ARN with the resolver prefix. This section explains how to centralize server access logs from several source buckets into one destination bucket. The destination bucket is named example-access-log-archive and is owned by account 555566667777. Add a statement with the Sid S3ServerAccessLogging that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-access-log-archive/source-logs/*. The Principal is arn:aws:iam::555566667777:role/BucketLoggingWriterRole, which is the role used to write the log objects. Add a StringEquals condition on s3:x-amz-acl set to bucket-owner-full-control. Add an ArnLike condition on aws:SourceArn with the value arn:aws:s3:::example-source-*, so that only the intended source buckets are covered. On each source bucket, enable server access logging with example-access-log-archive as the target and source-logs/ as the prefix. Log objects are written periodically, and delivery is best effort rather than guaranteed in real time. Confirm configuration by checking for a new object under the prefix after several hours of traffic.

This section explains how to centralize server access logs from several source buckets into one destination bucket. The destination bucket is named example-access-log-archive and is owned by account 555566667777. Add a statement with the Sid S3ServerAccessLogging that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-access-log-archive/source-logs/*. The Principal is the service principal logging.s3.amazonaws.com, which is the identity used to write the log objects. Add a StringEquals condition on aws:SourceAccount set to 555566667777. Add an ArnLike condition on aws:SourceArn with the value arn:aws:s3:::example-source-*, so that only the intended source buckets are covered. On each source bucket, enable server access logging with example-access-log-archive as the target and source-logs/ as the prefix. Log objects are written periodically, and delivery is best effort rather than guaranteed in real time. Confirm configuration by checking for a new object under the prefix after several hours of traffic.

This guide sets up a bucket to receive web firewall logs from the GateShield service. Create a bucket named example-firewall-logs, and note that GateShield requires a bucket name that begins with the string example-firewall. Add a bucket policy statement with the Sid GateShieldLogWrite and Effect Allow. Set the Principal to arn:aws:iam::909090909090:role/GateShieldLogDeliveryRole, which is the role GateShield uses to write on behalf of the web ACL. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-firewall-logs/gateshield/AWSLogs/909090909090/*. Add a second statement that allows s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:ListBucket on the bucket for the same role. In the web ACL logging settings, select the bucket as the destination and choose which fields to redact, such as authorization headers. Log files are written in JSON Lines format and are rolled every five minutes. If the destination validation fails, review the policy for typographical errors in the account ID.

This guide sets up a bucket to receive web firewall logs from the GateShield service. Create a bucket named example-firewall-logs, and note that GateShield requires a bucket name that begins with the string example-firewall. Add a bucket policy statement with the Sid GateShieldLogWrite and Effect Allow. Set the Principal to the service principal delivery.gateshield.amazonaws.com, together with an aws:SourceArn condition naming the web ACL in account 909090909090. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-firewall-logs/gateshield/AWSLogs/909090909090/*. Add a second statement that allows s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:ListBucket on the bucket for the same service principal. In the web ACL logging settings, select the bucket as the destination and choose which fields to redact, such as authorization headers. Log files are written in JSON Lines format and are rolled every five minutes. If the destination validation fails, review the policy for typographical errors in the source ARN.

This procedure describes how to export database audit logs from TableVault into a bucket on a daily schedule. Create a bucket named example-db-audit-exports and enable default encryption with a managed key. Add a bucket policy statement with the Sid TableVaultExportWrite and Effect Allow. The Principal is arn:aws:iam::303030303030:role/TableVaultExportRole, which the export job in that account uses to write files. Allow s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::example-db-audit-exports/daily/*, since large exports are uploaded in parts. Add a statement allowing s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket ARN for the same role. In the TableVault console, configure the audit export with the bucket name, the prefix daily/, and a 02:00 UTC schedule. Each export produces one object per database cluster, named with the date. After the first scheduled run, confirm that the objects exist and that no incomplete multipart uploads remain.

In the TableVault console, configure the audit export with the bucket name, the prefix daily/, and a 02:00 UTC schedule. Each export produces one object per database cluster, named with the date.
